meta.face: A Northumbrian of about sixty, stately and 'comely in person', with a fair, fresh, open complexion and a well-proportioned, SQUARE-OVAL face — a broad, smooth forehead, a straight nose of medium length with a slightly BROAD tip, LARGE, bright, LAUGHING blue eyes creased at the corners under fair, gently arched brows, FIRM, full cheeks with DIMPLES in a broad, frank smile that shows a little of the teeth, a STRONG, broad, CLEFT chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; fair hair gone silver in a neat ring around the tonsure; the look joyous and direct. Not the beak-nosed, long-chinned wilfrid (his master), the long, handsome, unsmiling oswald_worcester, the milk-white, full-oval edward_confessor, the broad, snub-nosed richard_chichester, the smooth, neat-nosed malachi_armagh or the long-headed, prim ludger.
meta.basis: The book, after Alcuin's Life, calls him 'stately and comely in person, frank and joyous, wise in counsel, pleasant in speech': hence a handsome, broadly smiling face. The pallium is from Wikipedia (Pope Sergius I, 695); the Frisian landscape follows Georg Sturm's painting on English Wikipedia and the book.
